hints: State the work-energy principle for downhill motion: $W_{\text{engine}} + \text{Loss in PE} = \text{Gain in KE} + W_{\text{res}}$.
Calculate the gain in kinetic energy: $\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}m(v^2 - u^2) = \frac{1}{2}(2500)(30^2 - 20^2)$.
Calculate the loss in gravitational potential energy: $\Delta E_p = mg(d\sin 4^\circ)$ with $d = 400\text{ m}$.
Calculate the work done against resistance: $W_{\text{res}} = R \times d = 600 \times 400 = 240000\text{ J}$, and solve for $W_{\text{engine}}$.
walkthrough:
State the work-energy principle for motion under engine power, gravity, and resistance:
$$W_{\text{engine}} + E_{p,\text{loss}} = E_{k,\text{gain}} + W_{\text{res}}$$

Calculate the increase in kinetic energy for mass $m = 2500\text{ kg}$ from $u = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$E_{k,\text{gain}} = \frac{1}{2}m(v^2 - u^2) = \frac{1}{2} \times 2500 \times (30^2 - 20^2)$$
$$30^2 - 20^2 = 900 - 400 = 500$$
$$E_{k,\text{gain}} = 1250 \times 500 = 625000\text{ J}$$

Calculate the loss in gravitational potential energy descending distance $d = 400\text{ m}$ on a $4^\circ$ incline:
$$h = d\sin 4^\circ = 400\sin 4^\circ$$
$$E_{p,\text{loss}} = mgh = 2500 \times 10 \times 400\sin 4^\circ = 10000000\sin 4^\circ$$
$$\sin 4^\circ \approx 0.06975647 \implies E_{p,\text{loss}} = 697564.7\text{ J}$$

Calculate the work done against the constant resistance force $R = 600\text{ N}$ over $400\text{ m}$:
$$W_{\text{res}} = R \times d = 600 \times 400 = 240000\text{ J}$$

Substitute all energy quantities into the work-energy balance:
$$W_{\text{engine}} + 697564.7 = 625000 + 240000$$
$$W_{\text{engine}} + 697564.7 = 865000$$
Subtract $697564.7$ from both sides:
$$W_{\text{engine}} = 865000 - 697564.7 = 167435.3\text{ J}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $167000\text{ J}$ (or $167\text{ kJ}$).
